access_links.label: Regione Piemonte: relocation from hydrogeological risk areas

dedupe_keys.name: preventive relocation buyout of households at high hydrogeological risk in piemonte italy climate adapt

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes Piemonte's preventive relocation scheme, the only one of its kind in Italy, which buys out homes in areas at high landslide, avalanche or flood risk that planning instruments have closed to further urban use. Since 2009 owners of primary and secondary homes can receive a relocation grant, calculated at up to EUR 1,034 per square metre (the regional cost ceiling for new subsidised social housing) for up to 200 square metres, then adjusted by a coefficient for residence type; the grant can buy or build a new home or serve as an indemnity, and the old building is demolished. Priority goes to primary homes, higher risk and less predictable hazards such as landslides and avalanches. The region budgets EUR 900,000 a year from state water-use fees. From 2009 to 2024 the scheme cost EUR 5,347,715.51: EUR 4,730,918.70 in purchases and EUR 1,116,868.66 in demolition. Coverage: the Piemonte region, where about 6% of land is at high or very high landslide risk. Access: the case study page, published on 22 October 2024 and modified on 25 August 2026, with the regional programme page in Italian. Licence: Climate-ADAPT content under the EEA reuse policy; free. Caveats: no formal cost-benefit analysis has been done, and the page gives costs, not the number of households moved. Simulation uses are parameterising managed retreat options and their costs in regional flood and landslide risk models. Related records: the Eferdinger Becken relocation case study.
name: Preventive relocation buyout of households at high hydrogeological risk in Piemonte, Italy (Climate-ADAPT)
outcomes: Since 2009 the region has paid relocation grants, capped at EUR 1,034 per square metre for up to 200 square metres, to owners of houses in high-risk zones, then demolished the buildings; from 2009 to 2024 the scheme cost EUR 5.35 million, of which EUR 4.73 million went to households and EUR 1.12 million to demolition.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study with Regione Piemonte and CMCC
